clue.text: It's not normal! No theologian youth leader has sex appeal!

parts.note: O is a nought, a zero, so it stands for none
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
IT is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so the opening letter of youth is taken

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation that a young religious scholar's charisma has been noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins the pieces; the youth leader goes on the end, after IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing or person that is abnormal or peculiar is a curiosity, an odd one.

clue.text: Illuminate tram with neon design

indicators.note: the letters are given a new design, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A tram is lit up with neon in a decorative pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges TRAM plus NEON. 'Illuminate' is here the old sense of decorating, as in an illuminated manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To illuminate a manuscript is to decorate it, to adorn it with embellishment.

clue.text: Most true stories tend to begin with dull opening

indicators.note: with dull opening says that piece comes at the front

parts.note: dead means dull or lifeless
lies are false stories

indicators.note: to begin asks for the first letter of tend only

explanation.surface: A complaint that true stories tend to start with a boring introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... opening' puts the dull piece first, and 'to begin' takes T from 'tend'. 'Deadly' can mean unerringly accurate, so 'most true' is its superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly aim is perfectly accurate, so the most deadly shot is the truest one.

clue.text: Ready for drive

parts.note: in golf the ball is set on a peg before the drive from the first stroke area

explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball placed on its peg is set up, prepared for a driving shot.

clue.text: Able to figure out true name

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone clever enough to work out a real name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRUE and NAME; 'figure' here means do sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent with numbers means one can do arithmetic, can calculate.

clue.text: Misshapen nut contains nasty gunge, not good for ointment

indicators.note: the first set of letters holds the second within it
a misshapen thing is bent out of form, so its letters are rearranged
nasty suggests the word is messed up and rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A deformed nut full of revolting goo is not a good thing to use as balm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from the goo, 'nasty' and 'Misshapen' each rearrange, and 'contains' sets the scrambled goo inside the scrambled nut.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing salve rubbed on the skin, a medicinal cream.

clue.text: Clearly elliptic, arranged with two unknowns

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: in algebra x and y are the usual unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Elliptic equations laid out plainly with two variables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ELLIPTIC together with X and Y, the algebraic unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in plain terms, leaving nothing implied, is saying it unambiguously.

clue.text: Courts publicise volunteers' return

indicators.note: return means the letters come back the other way

parts.note: to air a view is to publicise it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Law courts advertise that volunteers are coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AIR + TA backwards to make ATRIA. The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer army.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central halls or courtyards in Roman houses.

clue.text: Currency circulations

parts.note: reads like money changing hands, but currency is the state of flowing as a current, and the circulations are swirls in water

explanation.definitionFit: Whirlpools and swirls in a current of water or air are circular motions within a flow.

clue.text: Irregular sound, not quite complete

parts.note: sound means healthy, fit

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A noise that comes and goes, never quite whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise but means healthy; 'not quite' drops the last L of FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes in spasms and starts is uneven, spasmodic.

clue.text: Ordering nice starter to be consumed at home before grand opening

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last
a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of nice is used

parts.note: food that is consumed has been eaten
in means at home

indicators.note: opening asks for the first letter of grand

explanation.surface: Arranging a pleasant first course to be eaten at home ahead of a big launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' and 'opening' look like food and a ceremony but each take a first letter; 'before' sets the grand opening after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying something up is putting it in order, making it neat.

clue.text: Trimmed and separated out at last

indicators.note: out tells us to remove a letter from the word

parts.note: parted means separated

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of at

explanation.surface: Something cut back and finally taken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes T, the last letter of 'at', from PARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pared means cut back by shaving off the edges, as with fingernails or costs.

clue.text: Whisky shared by scholar and officer

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a scholar's degree
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A dram split between an academic and a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shared by' just joins MA and LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is a whisky made from malted barley, such as single malt Scotch.

clue.text: Turning fifteen, Mae is girlish

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Mae is reaching fifteen and growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like 'turning fifteen', an age, but rearranges FIFTEEN and MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effeminate describes a man with traits thought of as womanly, feminine.

clue.text: Suffering lady in a French story

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Suffering lady in a French story': A + F (French) + FICTION (story) gives AFFICTION, and no standard abbreviation lets 'lady' supply the missing L; the original clue could not be found
annotationWithheld.clue: Suffering lady in a French story

clue.text: Capital required

explanation.definitionFit: The needful is slang for money, cash to spend; needful also means necessary, called for.

clue.text: Boy in experiment concerning close-knit community

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a trial is an experiment or test
B is an abbreviation for boy, as in birth records

explanation.surface: A lad taking part in a study of a tight-knit group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B (boy) inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal means relating to a tribe, a close-knit social group bound by kinship.

clue.text: Something added to agreement

explanation.definitionFit: An accession is an addition, as a new item for a library; it is also consent, as a country's assent to a treaty.

clue.text: Transported without raising scandal — that's harsh!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the piece goes round the other

parts.note: transported means sent, conveyed or delighted

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: Someone carried away without stirring up gossip; that is a grating outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old meaning of outside, and 'raising' turns the scandal upward, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and grating, unpleasantly rough.

clue.text: It's vital I choose some writing style

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A writer insists on selecting a manner of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks a run of letters from 'It's vital I choose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic is a sloping typeface or script, a way of writing letters.

clue.text: Soldier in court about Asian communication system

indicators.note: about means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India, a means of communication

explanation.surface: A soldier at court discussing an Asian network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps one piece round the other. The Chindits were a British special force fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chindit was a member of Orde Wingate's jungle-fighting force in Burma.

clue.text: Predator tailing European mammal

indicators.note: tailing means following on behind, so this piece goes after

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
a cat is a predator

explanation.surface: A hunter stalking a European animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Predator' looks like the definition but is wordplay; 'tailing' puts it after the European. The polecat is a weasel-like animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred carnivore of the weasel family.

clue.text: Quite enough practise outside medical department

indicators.note: outside means this word wraps around the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to practise it
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Doctors have done enough practice outside the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the verb round the hospital department; ear, nose and throat is a standard hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means an ample amount, as much as is needed.

clue.text: Most special characters get top points

indicators.note: characters means the letters themselves, which are taken and rearranged
most of a word is all but its final letter

explanation.surface: The most unusual people reach the summits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims SPECIAL to SPECIA, and its 'characters' (letters) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Apices are tips or peaks, the highest points of things.

clue.text: Banned writing contains plagiarism, denied initially

indicators.note: contains means the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing
a crib is something copied or plagiarised

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of denied

explanation.surface: An essay was outlawed for copying, though the student denied it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts the copied work inside the writing, and 'initially' adds the first letter of 'denied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proscribed means forbidden or outlawed.

clue.text: Musical performance without first or last note

indicators.note: removing the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: A show of music missing the opening and closing notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first or last' strips the first and last letters from CONCERT. A oncer was British slang for a one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncer is old British slang for a one-pound banknote.

clue.text: First class road into Italian wine region

parts.note: A is first class, as in A1
ST is street, a road

explanation.surface: A major road leading into an Italian wine area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' only joins; A, ST and I are side by side. Asti is in Piedmont, home of sparkling Asti wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town and province in northern Italy famed for sparkling wine.

clue.text: Colour, new soldier doesn't start without it

indicators.note: without means the following letters are taken away
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a recruit is a newly enlisted soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh soldier cannot begin without colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops R from RECRUIT; 'without it' then takes away IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale beige or unbleached linen shade.

clue.text: Oddly chancy, this, for desert dwellers

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A risky venture for those living in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters of 'chancy' and 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulent plants that thrive in arid lands.

clue.text: Searching for the hidden Hammer or Spade?

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means investigative, seeking out what is concealed; Mike Hammer and Sam Spade are fictional private eyes.

clue.text: Force long suit

explanation.definitionFit: Strength is power or might; a long suit in cards, figuratively, is a person's strong point.

clue.text: Container craft going around New England

indicators.note: going around means one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat, a craft

explanation.surface: A boat sailing round the north-eastern US states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' wraps the boat round the region. A punnet is a small basket for soft fruit, as strawberries are sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small light basket or carton for soft fruit.
